highlights: Harvest by voice — a new hands-free screen under the + menu. Say the crop, then the count, then the weight, then "next" to save it and start the following one. Your usual harvest form is unchanged and still one row above it.
Every voice save says out loud what it saved, buzzes, and leaves an undoable row — and a save that cannot go through says so instead of quietly moving on.

Dictating a word no longer doubles it. The microphone echoes a word back a fraction of a second later, and the check that was meant to catch that was comparing the two spellings too strictly to notice.
Adding photos to a planting opens a sheet with room for several at once — the card's camera button is now the door to it
Each staged photo shows a thumbnail so you can drop the one you didn't mean to pick
Instagram sharing stages its temporary stripped copy of a photo in an unreplicated bucket, so that copy is genuinely deleted after posting instead of persisting in a second region.
Tap the number on the Untagged filter to review your unassigned photos one at a time and put each one on a plant
It remembers the plants you just used, so a garden walk collapses to one tap per photo
Skip leaves a photo for later, and Back reopens the previous one if you put it on the wrong plant
The planting card's photo button is back to one photo at a time — adding several there needs a proper sheet, which is designed but not built yet
Photos are now kept on your phone between visits instead of being re-downloaded every time you open the app cold. Measured with it on: a second visit went from 24 requests / 3,341 KB to zero.
The cache stores thumbnails only and clears out any full-size originals it had saved before, so it stays bounded — the 500-item ceiling is about 115 MB rather than the ~2 GB it could have been.
The Untagged filter now shows how many photos are waiting, so a batch you meant to tag later is visible instead of forgotten
A big batch no longer pushes the target picker off screen — the staged strip scrolls inside a fixed height
Photo Library takes a batch — pick up to 20 photos, choose one home for all of them, upload once
Or upload a batch with no target at all: they land under Untagged and you tag them one at a time afterwards
A photo that fails stays put with its reason, so a retry is one tap instead of re-picking everything
Add several photos to a planting at once — the camera button on a planting card now takes a whole handful
Log Event takes several photos at once too: pick a few in one go and they all attach to the same event
Each photo reports its own upload status, so one failure names itself instead of sinking the batch
Photos: the app was downloading full-size originals into thumbnail-sized boxes on four more screens. Measured on the Today page at your phone's geometry: 82,957,060 bytes before, 3,542,820 after.
The offline photo cache now stores thumbnails only, and evicts full-size originals it had already saved. It was storing ~4 MB originals with a 500-item cap and no byte limit.
A new CI budget fails the build if a screen's photo payload goes back over 4 MB, so this cannot silently regress.
Undo on an inventory quantity now restores the original number. It was landing on a stale value and saving the result, so a packet at 2 became 1 after a tap-and-undo.
Seed packets you have used up no longer appear as sowable. They move to a new 'Sowed previously' list on Sow Now that keeps the full packet record, and they no longer show on the Today card either.
Feed cards no longer appear a day late for a feeding logged in the evening. Plan generation was reading the last feed date in UTC while the read path used Eastern time.
Schema-contract coverage: the audit's blind spot for JOINed relations narrowed from 186 undeclared references to 114.
New standing gate pins the sow-window fall-through as unreached, so a legitimate data fix can no longer move a close date months later in silence.
Photos can now be shared to Instagram as well as Facebook, chosen per post — the Instagram half is built but not switched on yet
Search now finds a crop by its other name — cantaloupe finds your melons, zucchini finds summer squash, rocket finds arugula
Groundwork for sharing garden photos to Facebook and Instagram — not switched on yet
Seed packet pages open again — every seed item was showing 'Internal server error' instead of its details
Seed packet provenance — vendor, SKU and origin — now saves when you add seeds in the app instead of being silently dropped
The bottom tab icons are in colour again — Today, Garden, Harvests and Put-Up
Voice probe: the simulated search round-trip is now off unless you ask for it
The 'use this crop instead' button is now a full-size tap target
Rain from the weather station now logs itself every night
The public garden pages no longer show where in the property a planting lives
The sign-in page and link previews no longer carry our names or the town

Archived plantings finally have a home: a new Archived page reachable from the Garden action row lists everything you have archived, with its crop, status and archive date, and an Unarchive button on every row. Dictation no longer doubles a word when the recogniser echoes it back — the fix that was supposed to catch that only checked one case, and a phone recording finally showed the other. Also: pressing Enter twice while a harvest is saving no longer logs it twice, the mic is released when you navigate away mid-dictation, and links to a planting or event no longer route through a project URL
Restores the Lambda config drift guard, which had been failing since the weather-station config moved out of the public repo into an environment variable

Voice debug probe now runs the harvest commit layer for real: it shows what would have been saved, when each utterance settles, and whether the settle timer ever fires — plus an opt-in long-run mode for the 20-utterance outdoor fixture. Admin diagnostics only, no user-facing voice feature yet
Debug & smoke menu in More — every diagnostic page now reachable from the installed app, with live build, service-worker and API status; sow row icon no longer renders in browser link-blue
Sow Now is findable again: its own top-level row in the More menu, and the Today sow line is now tappable and moved off the top of the page

Design-system guard widened to 36 files and 4 rule classes; 25 new icons and 93 emoji routed to the SVG registry; app launch ~1.2s faster; 78% smaller warm load; Collection retry no longer blanks the app

Snap has a third choice: "Add to a planting". It attaches the photo to the planting and does nothing else — it does not become the planting's main picture, and it does not log an event. The two existing options are unchanged and still there; this sits beside them, one field and Save, as direct as "Update a photo". It turned out the app could already do this internally — "Update a photo" is this exact step plus one more, and "Log on a planting" is this exact step plus one more — so nothing new had to be built underneath, only a way in.

Seed packets now track their own germination rate. Enter how many seeds you sowed when you sow them, fill in how many came up whenever you get round to it, and the packet shows the percentage. It is held per packet rather than per variety, because packets of the same seed differ by age, vendor and lot — which is the whole reason the number is worth having.

Sow from the same packet more than once and it combines them, keeping each sowing listed separately with its own rate and date. That is deliberate: 80% in March and 45% in July from one packet tells you the packet is going over, and a single averaged number would hide exactly that. A packet you have never counted from shows nothing at all rather than 0%.

Every edit to a planting is now recorded — what changed, from what to what, and who did it. Until now the table holding every planting was the one thing in the app with no history at all, so a planting's dates could be changed with no way to see what they used to be. Nothing about saving changes; the record is kept behind the scenes.

Fixed a weigh-in bug that could save a harvest when you meant to type a digit. Since v4.51.0 the bottom row of the weight keypad — 0, the decimal point and backspace — sat underneath the Save button rather than above it, so a press that landed slightly low committed the entry instead. It happened from the very first weigh-in of a sitting, not just later ones, and the only way back was Undo.

The cause was a wrapping label. Putting the date and the Close button beside the planting name left that name about half as much width, so a longer one ran onto a second line — and in the fixed weigh-in layout every pixel the top row takes comes straight out of the keypad's space below it. The name is now kept to a single line and shortened with an ellipsis if it does not fit, which puts the keypad back where it was, with the full clearance above Save restored.

The planting chooser on Log Event was impossible to tap when the page first opened. The Save button floats over the bottom of the form, and at phone size it landed directly on top of the chooser — covering 28 of its 44 pixels. Every point across that field, tested end to end, was answering as Save rather than as the chooser. So the first thing you reached for did nothing, and on most of its width a tap actually saved the form instead. Scrolling freed it, which is why it looked intermittent. The page now nudges the chooser clear on the way in, and the invisible part of the Save bar has stopped intercepting taps meant for whatever sits beneath it.

Four controls on Log Event were too small to hit reliably. "Add details" was 16 pixels tall against the 44 the app requires everywhere else, "More event types" 24, "Flag an issue" 36, and every date and text box 41. They are all at 44 now. The size is written down in one place this time, and a check measures every control on the page rather than only the four that were reported — which is how a fifth one nobody had noticed got caught and fixed alongside them.

Opening the planting chooser no longer waits on the network. The list it shows was made about ten times lighter last release, but it was still fetched from scratch every single time you opened a log event or a weigh-in. It now shows the list you already had and checks for changes behind it, the same way the Garden tab and the planting pages already do.

The Garden tab now paints instantly when you come back to it. It had no cache at all, so every single visit re-fetched the whole planting list and re-signed a photo link for each of the 213 plantings that have one — about 450 KB, cold, every time. It was not sometimes slow; it was always cold, and the network decided whether you noticed. It now shows the list you already had while quietly checking for changes behind it.
This uses the cache the app already ships and was already using on the planting page, the location page, Today's care list and the photo wall. Garden simply was not one of its readers.

Fixed the intermittent "Unauthorized" that has been interrupting Snap sessions and the Harvests page. The app was occasionally sending a request with no sign-in credential attached at all, which the server can only refuse — so you would get turned away mid-save while being perfectly online, and the only way through was to back out of the session or close and reopen the app. It now refuses to send a request it cannot sign, quietly fetches a fresh credential instead, and retries once on its own. The interruption should simply stop happening rather than becoming something you work around.

When something genuinely does go wrong with the connection, the message now says so. "Unauthorized" reads like a problem with your account, which it never was — you will now see "You appear to be offline" when the phone has no signal, and a plain "Couldn't verify your sign-in, tap Retry" when it does.

The planting chooser and the lists behind it load about ten times less data. Opening the chooser — on a weigh-in, on any log event — was fetching the widest response the app produces: roughly 1.2 MB, including a freshly signed photo link for all 233 plantings and the full reference text for every variety. The chooser shows none of that; it is a list of names. It now asks for just the fields it draws, about 120 KB, and signs no photo links at all. Same list, same order, same behaviour.
This is the same fix the Garden tab already had. Garden was narrowed in an earlier release and the chooser was simply never included, which is why the two felt different.

The date is now on the weigh-in screen itself, next to the planting chooser, and it says "Today" or "Yesterday" rather than a raw date. It used to be buried inside the collapsed "Photo, notes & date" panel, which made logging yesterday's picking a chore. It also STAYS PUT between entries now: set it once at the start of a sitting and every save in that sitting is filed under that day. Outside a weigh-in session the ordinary log form is unchanged and still resets to today for each event.

The line at the bottom of the weigh-in screen now shows only the entry you just logged — its date, the planting, the count and the weight — on two lines. The running session count and running weight total are gone. They were crowding out the thing that line is for, which is checking that what you just put on the scale went in correctly; the numbers were also being pushed off the right edge underneath the Save button, so the half you most needed to read was the half you could not see.

The weigh-in session has a Close button, top right. The session deliberately hides the bottom navigation while you are in it, so there was previously no obvious way out other than the browser's own Back. If you have a weight typed in when you tap it, it asks before discarding it.

Logging a harvest no longer raises the "putting any of this up for later?" banner. Putting food up is its own sitting, done at the freezer, not something decided while a bowl is still on the scale — so the prompt was appearing at the one moment it could never be acted on, once per harvest. Put-Up is still reachable from its own tab and from any planting.

The weigh-in session no longer moves under your thumb. Every entry used to travel about 594 pixels up and down and land back exactly where it started — two separate scrolls fighting each other, one shoving the keypad clear of the Save bar and the other dragging the page back to find the chooser. The screen is now fixed: the planting chooser is pinned at the top, the fields and both keypads sit in the middle, and Save stays at the bottom. Measured across four entries, nothing scrolls at all.

The weight keypad was dead from your second entry onward, and this fixes it. As the session log grew, the Save bar grew with it and covered the bottom row of keys — including backspace. They still looked perfectly tappable and did nothing. There is now an enforced gap between the last row of keys and Save, checked automatically so it cannot drift back.

The session log is one line now, with the last ten behind a tap. It still shows what you just entered and still has Undo, both always on screen. The "+3 earlier" line finally does something — it was plain text with no tap handler before, so the log has never actually been able to show you more than three.
The bottom navigation bar hides while you are weighing in, and comes back when you leave. It was taking 68 pixels of a screen that had none to spare, and every button on it left the session.

There is a handedness setting now, under Settings. Set it to left-handed and the controls that matter move to the side your thumb actually reaches — including on the Today watch band, where the ten-to-twenty-day snooze was sitting under your left thumb while the harmless button sat out of reach. Backspace moves to the near column too. The digits never move.

Feed cards clear when you feed the plant. A heavy feeder in flower or fruit was recommended for feeding every single day regardless of when you last fed it — Armageddon sat on the list four days running with a feed six to nine days old against a seventeen-day interval, and came back the morning after you fed it.

A fertilizing you log today but date to an earlier day now checks off the Feed card. It never did before, so the card stayed up as though you had not done it. Watering deliberately keeps the calendar-day rule.

Six more places that failed silently now tell you. Unarchiving a project or a planting, archiving or deleting from the planting editor, undoing from the dashboard toast, and resolving a finding — all of them could fail with nothing on screen changing. The worst was the Undo strip after archiving a planting, which cleared itself before the request finished, so a failed undo destroyed its own second chance.
Discarding a Facebook caption or a photo's tags now asks first. Both surfaces threw the work away silently, and the caption box holds up to 5000 characters.

Put-ups understand four more methods — quick pickle, pesto, hot sauce and fermenting mash — and can now hold things that were never planted, like bread, cheese and butter. Your put-up view answers "where's my bread?" without pretending it grew in a bed.

Voice input no longer doubles a word. Saying "bitter melon" was giving you "bitter bitter melon", and it happened most when you enunciated carefully — because a clear pause makes Chrome decide "bitter" is a finished phrase, then change its mind a moment later and send the whole thing again. The app was treating the second version as new words and sticking it on the end. It now treats it as a correction and replaces what it had. The two earlier attempts at this fixed a different, rarer version of the problem.

Tapping the weight or quantity box during a weigh-in now brings up a number keypad instead of the full letters-and-numbers keyboard. The pad itself is unchanged. The redundant “Next” button on the quantity pad is gone — you can just tap the weight box, or keep using the pad.

Typing in a form and pressing Back no longer throws the work away silently. Add Planting, Edit Planting and Sow all ask first now, with a proper in-app confirmation rather than the browser's grey box. Sow was still unguarded before this — it kept nothing of what you had typed.

Each crop on Harvest Totals now shows a photo, taken from the planting of that crop you picked from most recently. 30 of your 31 crops already had a picture ready, so it looks complete rather than half-empty.
A jar you have finished no longer disappears from a planting's put-up list. It stays, marked as used, so the planting still shows everything it produced.
Deleting or archiving a project used to fail silently — you tapped, nothing happened, and nothing said why. It now tells you.
The greeting no longer calls Jen "Dave". It was a hardcoded fallback name, used whenever a first name was missing.

The planting chooser stops jumping. It decides whether to open upwards or downwards once, when you open it, instead of re-deciding on every frame while the keyboard slides up — which is why it sometimes flipped while you were already looking at it.
Both number pads now sit below their field instead of one above and one below, putting them a little closer to your thumb. Nothing got taller.
You can bring back a plant you snoozed with "Not yet". Until now that hid it for ten to twenty days and there was no way to undo it once you left the page.
Plants you grow to look at no longer pretend to be food. A pothos was showing a "Harvested" section and actively offering to log a put-up from it.
Rain that has actually fallen today now counts toward watering on the day it falls, rather than the day after. This affects the watering ledger, which is not switched on in production yet.

Projects you marked private were readable by anyone who had the link. The public share route served every project by its slug with no privacy check at all, and it handed back your notes, description, species and variety along with it — confirmed live against the previous version on a project whose is_public flag was false. It now refuses anything not marked public. If you have ever shared a link to one garden, that link could reach the others.

Harvest quantity and weight now have their own number pad, so the phone keyboard stays down. Tapping 3 still fills in 3 in one tap — that is most of your picks and it has not changed. What changed is everything else: 13 used to mean tapping into the field, waiting for the keyboard, and typing two digits. Now it is tap 1, tap 3. In a weigh-in session the keyboard never appears at all, which is where it had been covering roughly half the screen. There is a backspace key, and it matters more than it sounds: the pad BUILDS a number rather than replacing it, so a mis-tap adds a digit instead of overwriting one.
Add Planting opens as a fly-over on top of the Garden tab instead of a form wedged into the top of it. That was the last form still built the old way.

What you type into Add Planting or Edit Planting no longer vanishes if you back out. Both forms used to close on the Back gesture and throw away everything typed — no warning, and nothing to recover afterwards. They now ask first. Edit has been doing this since it became a fly-over three versions ago; it was never intentional.
The Harvest log no longer shows the same pick twice if you happen to be scrolling through it at the moment a new version goes out.
The microphone button on the notes and quantity fields is easier to hit. It looks exactly the same — the tappable area around it grew to the size it should always have been.
Search engines were being served the app's loading shell instead of a real robots.txt.

The Needs-care list on Today no longer moves under your finger. Working down a location group and tapping Log, the sections were quietly re-sorting themselves after every single tap — the list ranks groups by how overdue they are, and logging a plant lowers its group's score, so the page re-ranked itself mid-tap and slid the next plant somewhere else. That is why you were mis-tapping. The order is now fixed when the page loads and only changes when you change it; the same applies to which sections sit open, which were popping open on their own for the same reason.

The care rows are about a third shorter, so you see roughly 13 plants where you used to see 9. The green Log button is gone — the coloured water chip IS the button now. It was already telling you how urgent the plant was, and having a separate button next to it was two controls doing one job. Skip sits to its left, water on the right where your thumb is. The "1d overdue" line went with it: the chip's colour already says that, and it was costing a whole second line on every row. One consequence worth knowing — a 4-day and a 19-day overdue plant now look the same shade, since the colour has three bands rather than a number.
Each section on Today has its own "Water all" button in its header, so a group like Pasture Bag Area with 77 plants logs in one tap without leaving the page for Log Many.

Today stopped explaining its own arithmetic. "One bulk water covers 111 of these, 113" is gone, and the staleness note lost the half that justified itself — it still tells you when rows are being withheld, because that is the part you cannot see for yourself.

The Harvest page crop blocks went from five stacked lines to two. "7 weighed, 10 estimated" is gone everywhere it appeared, and the kilogram figure now rides on the same line as the cups and bunches instead of owning a row. The ≈ still marks a total that contains estimates.

The Garden tab has no harvest data on it at all any more — no "This season", no weight, no counts. It is the browsing surface; the Harvest tab is where harvests live. It also stopped fetching the whole-garden harvest total on every visit to display it.

The harvest log is finally in the order you entered things. Inside each day the entries were sorted by their internal id, which is a random string — so the within-day order was noise, not history. Measured before the fix: on 2026-08-24, 13 of 13 entries were in the wrong place; on 08-17, 39 of 39. It now sorts by when you actually hit save, and a harvest you backdate still files under its harvest date while sitting at the top of that day as the most recent thing you entered.

The Snap button goes straight to your photos. It used to open a screen whose only option was "Choose photo" — a tap that did nothing but ask you to tap again, and you hit it twice per burst because it came back after every save.
The weigh-in queue is gone from the weigh-in session, along with the two requests it made every time the session opened. The session itself is untouched.

Plants you grow to look at no longer claim a harvest. The rescued violet was showing "Est. harvest Oct 4 – Oct 24"; six plantings were doing that and fourteen were carrying a days-to-maturity figure. The app has always known which crops are not harvested — the Today ready-band and the harvest watcher both check — but the planting card never asked. It still tells you how long ago something was transplanted, which is the part that means anything on a houseplant.
Fixed a crash waiting to happen in the harvest post composer: a crop name containing a bracket or a plus sign would have taken the whole composer down.

The Put-Up tab can now start from a harvest you already logged. Under "Log a put-up" there's a short list of your recent picks — tap one and the crop, the variety, the planting and the amount all come across filled in, so putting up this morning's basil is two taps instead of five fields. It also quietly records which harvest the jar came from, which nothing has ever done: of 791 harvests logged this year, not one was linked to a put-up, so the app could never answer what actually happened to what you picked.

The amounts convert properly on the way across. The harvest log says "cup" and the put-up list says "cups" — the same for pounds — and where there's no honest match at all (a harvest weighed in kilograms, which the put-up form doesn't offer) it fills in everything except the amount rather than quietly converting it and presenting a guess as a measurement.

Put-Up has a proper "Log a put-up" button at the top of the page, the same way Harvests has its weigh-in button. And if you tap the wrong harvest, there's now a Change link to clear it — before this there was no way to see which harvest a put-up was attached to, let alone undo it.

You can now say whether a location is under cover, on the location itself. Until now the watering engine worked it out by NAME — anything called "Stable" or "House" counted as covered, and everything else was treated as open to the sky. That meant a low tunnel or a cold frame was credited with rain it never actually received, and renaming a location silently changed how its plants got watered. Coverage is now a proper setting you can edit, with three states: covered, open, or unset (which falls back to the old guess from the location type).

Rain on your fabric bags stopped counting entirely on hot days. The rule was meant to reduce how much credit a bag gets for rain when it's 85F or hotter — a bag in full sun does dry out faster — but it was zeroing the credit out completely instead of trimming it. At 84F a 5-gallon bag got three days of credit for half an inch of rain; at 85F it got none. So on exactly the days the garden was under the most stress, the app would tell you to water bags it had just watched get rained on. It now keeps a day of credit rather than throwing it all away.

The weigh-in queue no longer disappears when it fails to load. If the list of what's ready to pick couldn't be fetched — a dropped connection, a hiccup at the server — the section simply didn't render, which looks exactly like "nothing is ready today." You'd be standing in the garden holding produce being told there was nothing to weigh, when nothing had actually been checked. It now says so and gives you a retry, and if only part of the list failed it says the queue may be incomplete rather than claiming it's empty.
The variety picker now describes itself correctly to screen readers. It was pointing at a dropdown that never got rendered, so assistive tech was told to look for something that wasn't there.

Deleting a project could quietly reassure you it was safe. Before deleting, the app checks whether anything would be orphaned — but when that check itself failed, the warning was lost and you were shown the clean "nothing will be orphaned" path anyway. You'd confirm a permanent delete believing it had been checked. It now tells you the check failed, offers a retry, and withdraws the permanent-delete button entirely, leaving Archive as the way out. Deleting an event could also fail with no message at all; that now surfaces too.

Photos shared to Facebook now carry a description for screen readers, built from what the photo actually is — the crop, the variety, the planting — rather than a filename or a generic line. Where there isn't enough on record to say something true, it sends nothing rather than filler, because a wrong description is worse than none.
Moving an event to a different project now moves its photo too. The event was re-pointed and its attached photo was left behind on the old project.

Tomatoes stop vanishing from the harvest list. The app decided a plant was finished once it had gone unpicked for three times its usual gap — which for a tomato meant just nine days, while a bay laurel got ninety. So five tomatoes you were still watering and feeding had quietly dropped off the list you use to log a pick. Every plant that ever went past that mark turned out to be picked again later — ten out of ten — so the guess was wrong every time it mattered. Now nothing is written off before eighteen days, whatever its usual rhythm. Genuinely finished plants, like the scallions last picked in June, still stay off the list.

Opening a crop on the Harvests page no longer shows the same plantings twice. It listed them once by variety and again in the table underneath — the table has the first-pick date and the variety list did not, so the list went and the table stayed.

Your harvest post keeps what you wrote. Closing the composer used to throw the caption away, so anything typed and not sent straight off was gone. It now comes back when you reopen it — along with any lines you unchecked — and clears itself once the post has actually gone out.
A Today filter on the photo library. With 1,300 photos in there, the one thing you want before posting is what you shot today, and that was the one cut you could not make.

Taking a photo inside the app is gone — every photo button now goes straight to your photo picker. The in-app camera could never save a shot to your camera roll (a web app has no way to write there), so the one place it was still offered was the one place a photo could quietly end up nowhere but here. Snap, Log Event, the photo library and every planting and location page now open the picker in one tap instead of asking take-or-choose first.

Every column in an opened crop now sorts. Tap Planting, Count, Total weight or First pick on the Harvests page to reorder just that crop's plantings — it opens alphabetically by plant name, and sorting one crop leaves the others alone.

The Today tab and the “given away” event have their own icons now. Today was drawing the same sprout as a seedling — and as sprouting, seeding and transplanting — so it is a checklist instead, which is what that page actually is. Giving plants away was drawing the identical symbol to the Share button, so it is a gift now. And the planting edit form no longer closes if you tap away while a save is still going through.

Editing a planting works again — and now opens right where you are. Tapping Edit on a planting used to send you to the Garden tab, and since 17 August it had been landing there with no form at all. It now opens as a fly-up on the planting page itself. Put-Up has its own tab instead of hiding under More. Log Many no longer skips plantings that aren't in a project. And a couple of help hints that were written but never shown now actually appear.

Privacy: photos taken in newer phone formats (HEIC and AVIF) now have their location and camera data removed, the same as every other photo — until now those formats were uploaded and shared exactly as the camera wrote them. Sharing to Facebook uses that same thorough cleaning too, including the extra data some phones tack on after the end of the picture.

Care, privacy and access: edits to an event or a plant merge now record who made them, so your changes and Jen's can be told apart. A photo whose location data cannot be removed is no longer shared. The photo library remembers which location you were filtering by. The photo buttons can be reached and used from a keyboard. And an event now always belongs to the same project as its planting.

Harvest, care and privacy: photos now ride along when you share a harvest — with location data stripped from every photo on upload and on share. Weigh-in sessions no longer restore an unrelated parked draft. Finished and failed plantings are out of Log Many. Search results open in place. Germination dates record the day you mean, not the day you logged it.

Dormant plants no longer clutter Log Many. Christmas cactus, Cavendish strawberries, wild wineberry, asparagus and garlic were all still turning up in bulk logging while fully dormant and needing nothing. They now drop off routine care lists — but stay in the Harvests tab, keep their own planting page, and can be brought back with a Resume button when they wake up.

Half-typed entries survive a reload. Every form in the app — planting editor, field capture, locations, tasks, project types, photo library, event detail, and the Facebook caption box — now holds on to what you were typing instead of losing it if the page reloads.
Harvest crop totals now show a count and a first-pick date beside the weight, so 65 fruit and 8.23 kg sit on the same line. Plantings logged by weight show a dash rather than a misleading number.
Tapping Harvest anywhere — the header or your home-screen shortcut — now opens the weigh-in session instead of the single-entry form.

Fixes: the Today watch list read the wrong days-to-maturity basis for cultivars that disagree with their crop; a timer on Add Inventory could fire after you left the page; and the coverage safety check could silently pass a real regression.

You can now record a plant you lost or one you gave away. Until now a planting that died, got eaten or went home with a neighbour had nowhere to go — you either ended the whole planting or let the count quietly drift. There is now a proper entry for it: say how many, and say what happened. For a loss the reasons are pests, disease, weather, transplant shock, animal damage, culled, or simply unknown; for a give-away they are a friend, donated, a plant swap, sold, traded, or shared locally. Both are required, because a count with no reason tells you nothing next spring. When a reduction takes a planting down to nothing, the app offers to close it out with the ending it thinks fits — you can take it, choose a different one, or wave it away and leave the planting open.

Photos load faster and stop swapping themselves out. A thumbnail that had to be refreshed was coming back as the full-size image, so scrolling a photo-heavy page pulled down far more than it needed to and pictures visibly jumped as they resettled. Each picture now asks for the size it actually wants and keeps it, and the app no longer confuses two sizes of the same photo for one another.

The app behaves itself when you are offline or signed out. Opening it with no connection could leave you on a blank screen indefinitely, waiting on a sign-in check that was never going to answer. It now waits a sensible moment and then gets on with it, showing you what it has saved rather than nothing at all. Separately, the offline store is now kept strictly per person, so there is no way for one household member's saved pages to appear under the other's name — and if the app cannot tell who you are, it saves nothing rather than guessing.

The "compose tonight's post" band on Today is back. It has not appeared at all since it was added: it was asking the server for the season's totals in a form the server rejects, and because the band is deliberately quiet about errors it simply never drew itself. Log a few harvests and it will now offer you the written-up list again.

Every screen now has the same header. Today, Garden, Harvests, Findings and Dashboard used to show a wide search box under the title, while every other screen showed search as a small round button beside Snap and Harvest. Those five now match the rest — three small buttons, no search box. They keep their titles and gain no back arrow, because a back arrow on a main tab has nowhere sensible to go.

The header is also shorter on those five screens, which gives back about 36 pixels of the page to what you actually came to look at. The title lettering was re-checked against the photo backdrop at the new height so it stays readable over a bright picture.

What you have typed into a form is no longer thrown away when the app reloads itself. The app updates in the background and can reload the moment a new version lands — and until now that reload did not care whether you were halfway through logging a harvest, sowing a packet, or recording a put-up. Whatever was on screen was simply gone. Those three forms now hold the reload until you are done, and keep a copy of what you had typed in case anything else interrupts.

The same protection now covers five more places where you enter things: the capture flow, field capture, adding inventory, starting a project, and adding seeds. Every one of them could previously lose what you had entered to a background reload or a stray tap on the backdrop.

Watering depth is no longer silently dropped. When you set a depth on a batch of waterings and then left the form, the depth was not saved with the rest of your draft — so it came back empty and the form did not even consider itself unfinished. It is now kept with everything else.

A new put-up is no longer attached to an old harvest. If you started a put-up from a harvest, left, and later opened a fresh one from scratch, the app quietly reused the previous harvest's link — filing your new batch against the wrong pick. A blank put-up now starts genuinely blank, while resuming one you started from a harvest still works as before.

Fertiliser products stop disappearing. Recording what you fed a plant worked, but any later edit of that entry — fixing a typo, correcting the date — wiped the product name out. Worse, the product was never shown anywhere unless you opened the edit screen, so it vanished without a trace. Edits now leave it alone, and it is visible on the entry itself.

Photos now record when they were actually taken. Every photo in the app until now had no capture time at all — the resize that shrinks a picture before upload was quietly stripping that information off it first, so the moment a photo was taken was destroyed on the phone and could never be recovered. The capture time is now read from the original before the resize touches it. Photos that genuinely have no capture time — screenshots, downloads, anything already stripped by a messaging app — stay blank rather than being given a made-up date.

The planting picker can be dismissed. On the log-a-harvest path the picker opened by itself and then could not be closed: it never took keyboard focus, so tapping away did nothing. There is now a close button, and Android's Back closes it too, without losing what you had already typed.

A planting with more than 50 harvests no longer understates its own total. The planting page asked for one page of harvests and used whatever came back, so past fifty picks the total on screen quietly stopped counting. It now reads the full, uncapped total the server already calculates. Your Pineapple Tomatillo was days away from crossing that line.

Editing a harvest keeps its weight consistent. Logging a harvest recorded the weight in two places; editing one afterwards only updated one of them. One record in the garden had already drifted this way — 35 in one field and 1 in the other.

Plantings can no longer be permanently and wrongly ruled out as too-late-to-mature. A behind-the-scenes check compared the expected maturity date against a deliberately cautious frost date rather than the real one, and anything it flagged was both hidden from the harvest watch list and skipped by the nightly recheck — so a wrong verdict stuck forever. Three plantings, including a Sweet Potato, have been put back.

A planting watered every day now reads as a daily cadence instead of a growing debt. Before, a once-a-day planting re-entered the watering list every calendar morning and carried an 'overdue by N days' count — but on a daily plant that number just means N days went by, not that the plant is behind. Eighty-two of your plantings were in that state, so a third of the garden rendered as urgent all the time and the urgent styling stopped meaning anything. Daily plantings now say 'Daily — due today', the list tells you how many one bulk watering covers, and nothing is hidden. No watering interval changed.

Big fabric grow bags now get rain credit the way beds do. A mulched, ground-contact fabric bag of 3 gallons or more behaves much more like a bed than like a nursery pot, so a modest rain now counts toward it. Seventy-six of your eighty fabric bags qualify. Rigid plastic pots, tray cells, hanging baskets and anything whose container is unrecorded are deliberately unchanged — they dry out faster and the old, stricter rule is right for them.

Troughs, whiskey barrels and large ceramic pots are no longer treated as small vessels. The watering rule had no idea how big a container was, so a six-foot trough got the same daily floor as a five-gallon pot. Six plantings move off a daily cadence. Fabric bags are excluded on purpose: your own cultivar notes were written for the bag each plant is actually in and still call for daily water in summer.

Ginger is now warned about at 55°F, not at frost. Tropical plants take cumulative, irreversible chilling damage in the low fifties, weeks before the first frost — so a frost-based alert arrives far too late to be useful. The planting page can also now flag containers whose type or size is missing or looks wrong, so you can correct them as you walk past.

You can now mark a planting as overwintering, from the planting page. Pick one of four regimes — under cover and still growing, cold and resting, hardy and out in the ground, or held indoors and tender — and the watering schedule changes to a reduced check rather than either normal watering or nothing at all. Clearing it puts the planting straight back to normal care.

Fall sowing dates for frost-hardy crops are now based on when frost actually arrives here. The app had been using a deliberately cautious late-September date as if it were the real first-frost date; measured over eleven years, the first freezing night at this site has never come in September, and the median is 29 October. Hardy sow windows move about three days later. The cautious date is kept where caution is the right answer — frost alerts still use it.

The app starts faster. It now warms up the server while it is waiting for sign-in to complete, instead of leaving that time idle, and stops downloading a piece of the sign-in interface on every single launch.
A weight typed into the harvest panel is no longer lost if you back out. It is saved with the rest of the draft and restored when you come back.

Groundwork for overwintering. The app can now treat a planting you're overwintering as its own care state — checked on a reduced schedule rather than either watered normally or ignored entirely, because a dry freeze kills more overwintered plants than the cold does. Nothing changes on screen yet: there is still no way to mark a planting as overwintering, so no planting is in that state. That part comes next.

Overwintering deliberately does NOT use the planting Status field. An overwintered kale is still vegetative and still growing — recording 'overwintering' in Status would have erased that, and Status has no automatic way back, so anything put into it tends to stay there.

You can now create a new crop type from the variety edit screen. Before this, minting a type was only possible while creating a brand-new variety — so a plant already in the app, like the Kousa Dogwood, could be edited forever and never get a type.

The crop-type chooser now has a search box, and "+ New crop type" sits at the top instead of below all 141 existing types. Finding a type, or discovering you can add one, no longer means scrolling a list the length of a phone book.

Harvest totals can be sorted by name, weight or number of picks, in either direction — and name is the default again. Ranking by weight answers "what produced?"; sorting by name answers "where is my chard?", and the list now does both instead of only the first.
The same sort applies inside a crop, so the varieties under Tomato reorder with it.
Rain is now credited by how much actually fell — a light shower and a downpour no longer count the same toward watering.

Sweet potato's storage deadline moved from October 15th to October 10th. The old date was set by soil temperature; the real limit is frost killing the vines, after which the roots start to go regardless of how warm the ground still is. Eleven years of recorded nights at the garden put the first freeze between October 10th and November 8th, so the window is tighter than the old date allowed but nowhere near as early as a first draft of this change assumed.

Harvest and Snap now live in the top bar, on every screen, as big easy-to-hit targets. Logging a harvest went from two taps to one, and Snap looks the same everywhere instead of a plain icon on Garden and a green pill on Today.
The Log harvest row left the + menu, since the new header button reaches the same form from anywhere. The menu is back to four items and 'Log an event' mentions harvests again.

Snap leads with Choose photo now. Photos taken inside the app can't be saved to your camera roll — that's a limitation of what a web app is allowed to do, not a bug — so the app no longer nudges you toward the option that quietly loses the picture everywhere else.

Skipping a care item now sticks. It used to be forgotten as soon as the tab closed, so you would skip watering something, come back a few minutes later, and find it asking again. Skips now also follow you between your phone and your laptop.
Log Many remembers whether you like everything pre-selected — per person, not per device. Dave and Jen can finally disagree about it on the same phone.
The What's New dot clears everywhere once you've read the notes, instead of following you to your other device.

Four cold-hardy salad greens are now proper crop types you can plant: Mache (Corn Salad), Claytonia (Miner's Lettuce), Tatsoi and Mizuna — each with its own harvest style, so the app knows Mache is picked once and Claytonia keeps regrowing.
Estimated harvest windows no longer carry the · site-calibrated tag. The maths behind the dates is unchanged; the label was advertising a precision you weren't asking for.

The "Last 7 days" harvest number was wrong, and badly — it read 50 when you had actually picked 163. It was counting only the newest page of records, which covered about three and a half days, and the top-crop line beside it came from that same short slice. Both now count the whole week.

Harvest weights now break down by variety and by individual planting, not just by crop. The lists are also ordered by how much you actually grew instead of alphabetically — Cherry Falls was sitting above Moskvich Heirloom on the one screen whose question is which produced, on 763 g against 8,233 g.

The season total now tells you how much of the poundage is estimated rather than weighed — 52% right now. The old "313 weighed · 367 estimated" read as mostly-weighed, because the picks you weigh tend to be the small ones.

Treating a pest now checks the task off. "Doctored" has quietly become the thing you actually log — 239 in the last 30 days, against none for the older "pest treatment" — but the care list only recognised the old one, so a treated plant kept asking to be treated.

Today's care list now opens on the group with the most work in it, rather than the one holding the single most-overdue row. It had been opening on a 4-item group while 116 items — 60% of the list — sat folded away behind collapsed headers.

When watering records have gone stale across the board, the app now says so instead of presenting a 200-item backlog as though every one were genuinely due. Long water lists also cap at 20 per group behind a "Show more", which never affects the bulk action.

Each planting shows when it was last watered, right beside its due state. Opening Details from the photo also stops bouncing you back to the Basics tab, so the Care tab finally stays where you put it.

Fall sowing windows now work off real crop hardiness instead of matching words in the variety name. Spinach, every lettuce, Vates and Redbor kale, mustard, arugula, chard and leek were all missing the cold-hardy grace period they had earned — and Lacinato and Vates kale, the same species and equally hardy, disagreed by 12 days purely on how someone had worded the name. Six crops came off the "too late" list.
The sow-next-year section no longer describes itself as flowers. It is a timing section — overwintered kale belongs in it just as much as the hollyhocks do.
Aloe, calibrachoa and lantana are now recorded as things you do not harvest, so they read as a decision already made rather than as missing data.

The app asks the browser to hold on to your offline data from the moment it opens, instead of only if you had visited field mode. Chrome on Android discards best-effort storage wholesale when the phone runs short on space.

Garden tiles were downloading full-size camera originals — about 71 MB for one screen of 24 plantings. They now use the small versions that already existed, around 5 MB for the same screen. Same picture, thirteen times less to load.
The plantings picker opens ready to type, instead of making you tap the field first. The old browse-without-the-keyboard mode is still there behind the keyboard button, which now toggles both ways.

The ready-to-pick tray in a harvest session no longer swallows the screen. With the keyboard open it could take the whole viewport and push the weigh-in form out of sight; it now holds to about half, and long planting names can't push it past that.
The rain gauge now also rejects a negative daily total. It already refused impossible highs; a day of negative readings was quietly collapsing to a truthful-looking 'no rain'.
Harvest anchors are re-derived nightly, so a planting whose sowing or potting-up date arrives later gets an updated estimate instead of keeping the one guessed on the day it was added.
Today was asking the server for your full planting list two or three times over on a single screen, once per block that needed it. It now asks once and shares the answer.
Your planting list was being sent uncompressed — about 580 KB of text per request. It now compresses, which is roughly a fifth of the size over the wire. Most noticeable on mobile data.

Plantings can now be marked as having arrived already grown — a nursery plant or a set, rather than something started here. Nothing shows this in the app yet; it currently keeps those plants from skewing the harvest-window estimates for everything else.

Fixed: merging two plantings moved the events across but left the surviving plant's "last watered / last harvested" summary frozen at its old dates. Five plants were showing stale dates — Cilantro since July 31 — and have been corrected. Merging now rebuilds the summary.
Ambient bands now say when they could not check, instead of quietly looking empty. A one-off blip on a waking phone still shows nothing; only a real outage puts a line on Today.

Harvest-window estimates re-fitted on a full season of your own picks — 35 plantings now, up from 18, with taste-picks and probes filtered out. Windows sit about a week later than before and land right 31 times out of 35.
A brand-new planting gets its harvest anchor straight away instead of waiting for the next backfill, including plantings that belong to no project.
Harvest weights: a jalapeno-type pepper was carrying a 5 g catalogue figure against your own 43 g and 56 g weighings. Corrected, and the whole stored weight corpus re-derived from your measurements.

Quieter fixes: the rain gauge now rejects a physically impossible daily total instead of reading a broken tipping bucket as real rain, and the app can no longer cache an error page in place of a photo or a script.
Snap now offers a link to the record you just captured
Harvest windows stay open on repeat crops, transplant events set the anchor, and weight samples follow a planting's identity
Harvest weight by crop on the Garden, and derived anchors retire when a real date arrives
Logging a harvest now moves the planting to Harvested automatically
Plantings you have marked as fruiting now open their own harvest-watch row
Harvest watch list now includes plantings that aren't in a project
Harvest export and the Harvests page gain Today and Yesterday chips, so you can pull just tonight's picking — or last night's, after the fact

The harvest export log now groups by day, then crop, then variety, instead of one flat list per day. Repeat pickings of the same variety on the same day fold into one line, and amounts in different units stay separate rather than being added together
Tapping the harvest quantity field now pulls the Harvest panel to the top of the screen, so the quantity, weight and Save button stay above the keyboard
After saving a harvest, the page scrolls back to the planting picker instead of leaving it above the top of the screen

Plantings with no recorded sow or transplant date can now enter the harvest watch list using a derived estimate, so they stop being invisible. Derived estimates rank below real dates and never displace them
Snap can now log a photo against a location — a bed, area or structure — instead of forcing it onto a nearby planting it was not a photo of
Duplicate plantings combined — 15 double-entered plantings folded into their originals, keeping the full combined history, photos and harvests

Your Dashboard total-events count drops by 492. Those were duplicate rows created when one bulk action was logged separately against each duplicate — no harvest, photo or weight was lost, and harvest totals are unchanged
Merged plantings now keep the most-advanced live stage: a planting whose sibling is still fruiting no longer reads as 'harvested'
Every merge records a full before-state snapshot, so any of them can be reversed
Weigh-in queue now also lists your recently picked plantings, not just the ones the readiness model expects — so the tray is never empty when you have harvests to weigh.

Weigh-in session: pre-flight queue. Tap the plantings on your counter in order — the form fills itself, and each save advances to the next one with the cursor already in Quantity. Enter hops Quantity → Weight, and Enter on Weight saves, so a pile is: type count, Enter, type grams, Enter.
Weigh-in session mode for harvests. Open the log in session mode from the Harvests page and record a run of weights back to back, instead of walking the whole log-an-event flow once per item.

Log Many can carry a note. One note for the whole batch — 'side-dressed the whole bed' — and the field says so, so it is never ambiguous whether it applies to one plant or thirty. It could not be added before now: the batch endpoint would have accepted the note and silently thrown it away behind a success screen.

Storage crops warn you before the window closes. Crops you harvest once and store — sweet potatoes, winter squash — have a real 'dig by this date or lose it' deadline that the app could not express anywhere. It appears on Today only when a deadline is genuinely near, and stays silent otherwise. Right now that means it shows nothing: the only sourced deadline opens October 1.

Housekeeping under the floor: a legacy tag table that nothing had read for months is gone along with three triggers that still fired on every delete; archived events can now be restored with their photo links intact; and a container can no longer be deleted out from under the containers nested inside it.
The Garden filter row is one tap instead of twelve chips. Twelve facet chips wrapped into a scrap-heap on a phone screen; they are now a single selector, ordered type, then location, then lifecycle.

Snap can finally add a plant it has never seen. Its two-field form was an outlier that could not create a variety or a crop type, so a genuinely new plant — hydrangeas, say — could not be captured at all. Snap now uses the same planting form as everywhere else, and still saves in the same number of taps: type a name and go.

Logging a date no longer invents a time you did not enter. Log Event offered a time field, threw the time away before saving, and stamped noon UTC on instead — which is why 545 of your harvests carry an identical placeholder timestamp. Both logging screens now ask for a date, and mean it.
Log Many and Log Event share one layout. Same sections, same order, same date control, instead of two forms that drifted apart.

Deleting or renaming a location by name can no longer hit the wrong one. Two locations under different parents may legitimately share a short name; the app now resolves to exactly one row, or tells you it was ambiguous, instead of quietly writing to every match.

Critters have gone quiet. The arrival animations and the little sprites on your Garden tiles are hidden — they had become visual noise on the screens you use to actually get work done. Nothing about earning them changed: every critter still triggers, logs and accrues exactly as before, and they are all still there in the collection.

Back now keeps your place everywhere it should. Container pages and the Harvests log join the photo library and feed — and Harvests brings back your filters and which view you were on, not just the scroll position, so a Back no longer dumps you on Totals.

Container event counts tell the truth. The number beside a container's event log counted archived events the log itself no longer shows — on eight containers it disagreed, and on four of them it promised events over a completely empty log.

Retake is beside the photo instead of below everything. On a 360px screen it was sitting 22 pixels below the fold, so deciding whether to keep a shot meant scrolling past all four destination cards first.

You can delete a single photo. Until now the only way to remove a blurry shot or a duplicate was to delete the whole event it was attached to, which threw away a real record to get rid of an image. The delete discloses what else it affects, and the photo goes to Recently Deleted where you can restore it.

Hitting Back keeps your place. The photo library and the feed now reopen exactly where you left them — same scroll position, and just as importantly the same number of items loaded, so the page you come back to is the page you left rather than a short one you have to scroll through again.

Harvest weights now say where the number came from, on the phone. The provenance was always there, but only as a hover tooltip — and there is no hover on Android, so on the only device this app is actually used on it was invisible. Every harvest weight now reads its basis as plain text: "typical for this variety", "your weighings", or "weighed" when it was a real measurement.

Your harvest totals will drop slightly, and that is the fix, not a loss. Archived plantings were leaking into normal views — 932 events, 28 photos, 4 harvests and their 424 g of weight were being counted in totals they should never have been in. Nothing was deleted; archived things are simply no longer counted as current.
Event pages are worth opening now. An event shows its planting, the amount and weight you logged, and its photos — instead of repeating the event type three times and telling you little else.
Container event logs no longer stop at 50. Busy containers page through their full history; the largest here holds over five thousand events.
Archive a planting straight from its page, and see how many you planted. No more opening the edit form to archive, and the count (×6 zucchini, ×30 basil) sits on the planting itself.

The planting picker works with a screen reader. It claimed to be an accessible combobox without implementing one; now the arrow keys, Escape and focus all behave, and it announces the option you are on.
Harvest seasons run November to October, matching how a growing year actually works rather than the calendar. Nothing you can see changes today — it starts to matter with the first November harvest.
Deleting something that is already gone no longer shows an error. It just closes, the way it always should have.

Recently deleted now covers everything, not just photos. Deleted containers, plantings, locations and cultivars are listed there with a Restore button each — 68 things that previously had no way back. Containers are listed first on purpose: restoring one brings the plantings inside it back into view.

Nothing looks different, but your garden data got a lot harder to lose. Deleting a bed, a container or a cultivar can no longer quietly take your photos, plantings, tags, earned badges or put-up records with it — the database now refuses instead of silently tidying up. Deleted locations and plantings can also be listed and restored again.

Voice dictation stops repeating (and stops dropping) words when you speak into notes. Signing out from the More menu behaves. Under the hood: the watch list learned to use derived planting dates, still switched off pending a look.

A calmer garden list: the 'ready to pick' block is gone from Today, plant names there now open the planting, and Android Back closes the More menu instead of jumping tabs. Harvest units stop sticking when you switch plants, and the crop picker puts your most-logged crops up front without burying the plant list.

Harvest lists you can trust: 'Not yet' snoozes a plant for 10 days, hidden rows expand in place, and every planting page gets a quick Log button. Photo-aware delete confirmations, editable watering depth, and smarter weather groundwork under the hood.

Today no longer says “All set — no watering needed” above a full watering list. The headline and the plant list now read the same rain thresholds, so they cannot disagree again, and forecast rain no longer talks you out of watering a container.

New “Worth checking” list on Today: a short list of plantings whose window may be opening, phrased as a prompt to go look rather than a claim that something is ready. Tap “Not yet” to clear a row — with an undo if you mis-tap.
Watering now records how much: Light, Normal or Deep, preset to Normal. Works on a single log and on Log Many, where you can set one amount for the batch and override any row.
New “Soil check” event for when you look at a plant and it does not need water. It counts as attention paid — today’s list clears — but earns nothing, so it can never be farmed.

You can delete a photo now, and get it back: deleting tells you plainly if it is a cover photo, never removes it from anywhere silently, and everything lands in a new Recently deleted page you can restore from.
Fixed a live bug where moving a photo to a different planting left the old one showing a cover photo it no longer had.
The app starts faster and stops flashing white on the way in — the opening screen now waits for the app to actually be ready instead of a fixed timer, and paints immediately on a cold start.
The plantings list loads roughly 190× faster on the screens that open it, including every time you open a log form.
Event history no longer stops at 50 — you can page back through a planting’s full log.
The harvest unit now pre-selects your crop’s usual unit, so logging in the wrong unit is harder.
Notes moved to the bottom of the log form, collapsed, so Save is closer to your thumb.
Removed the Plants | Photos switch from Garden — Photos has its own place in the menu.
Log a harvest straight from the + button — it is the first action in the create sheet now, and the planting picker opens ready for you, so a quick-button harvest is five taps with no typing.

The planting field no longer quietly fills itself in with whatever you logged last. You pick the planting each time; the one you used most recently is listed first, so it is one tap, not a silent guess.
New crop filter chips on the planting picker — tap Tomato or Pepper to cut a long list down instantly, and the filter stays put while you log a run of harvests.
Harvests now opens on Totals, the view you actually want on arrival. Coming in from a planting's 'All harvests' link still lands on the log, unfiltered by season.
Pick any past growing season from the season chip, and each crop's Totals row now carries a small sparkline of when it came in across the year.
New Export on Harvests: copy your totals or your log as plain text, filtered by crop and timeframe — totals break down by variety, with first-pick dates.

Harvest colour windows are live on the planting card: every colour you can legitimately pick at and what each one buys you in heat, sweetness or keeping — plus how to tell ripe from unripe on the varieties that ripen green.
Fixed: on Snap, the 'Retake / choose photo' button did nothing once you had already picked a photo. It works now, including when you pick the same photo again.
Fixed: dictating into a text box sometimes repeated words you had not said. Voice entry no longer double-counts a phrase the browser sends twice.

'Save to device' has been removed from Snap and from Log event. A web app cannot actually save into your phone's photo gallery — the button only ever opened a share sheet — so it was promising something it could not do.

Fixed: on the harvest form the unit box was squeezed so narrow you could not tell which unit was selected — it showed as just an arrow. The 1-6 quick buttons now spread across the full width of the row, and the unit sits next to the quantity where you can read it.
Harvests is now one of the five buttons along the bottom. DrG has moved into the More menu — it is still there, just not taking up a permanent slot.

Logging a harvest puts the things you actually fill in first: the planting, then how many, then the unit. Photo, notes and the date have moved together under one 'add details' section you can open when you need them. Every other kind of event keeps the order it had.

After you save a harvest the form stays open, ready for the next one. There is no longer a card to tap past, so logging several in a row is one tap shorter each time. A green strip confirms what you logged and carries an Undo, and a Done button closes things out when you are finished.
Fixed: saving a harvest no longer immediately shows a red 'Choose a planting' warning underneath the box you had just used.

Projects are no longer a thing you have to think about. The project chooser is gone from the logging form, the Garden groups by crop type instead of by project, and project names have been removed from breadcrumbs, the dashboard and the harvest list. Your data is untouched — every planting still belongs to the same place behind the scenes, and nothing was deleted.
When you log an event, the app now works out which project it belongs to from the planting you pick, instead of asking you first.
If you had projects saved as favourites, that section is hidden rather than removed — it comes back if this is ever reverted.

Dormant plants are now excluded from everything that suggests care. They were already kept out of the daily watering/feeding/pest lists, but three other places still counted them: the frost alert, the Findings list, and the dashboard needs-attention flag. Dormant stock sits in controlled storage and never needs that treatment.
The frost one mattered most — it is a real alert that emails you, it fires year-round on a temperature threshold, and nothing would have revealed the problem until the first cold night.
The Findings list also stopped suggesting care on plantings marked failed (7 of them were doing exactly that).

Fixed: a plant added with Snap could be found in search but tapping the result did nothing. Plants added that way have no project attached, and every link to them was built to require one — so the row looked tappable and was inert. Search, Favourites and the Last-harvest tile now link to the plant directly.

Fixed: opening the app from the home-screen “Log a harvest” shortcut no longer greets you with a message about a photo not carrying over. There was never a photo — the warning was firing on every single launch of the fastest way into the app.
Log Many now says up front that harvests are logged one at a time and why (each needs its own quantity), instead of silently bouncing you to the single-event form after you tap Harvested.

Logging a harvest now has quick-pick buttons for 1 through 6 right above the quantity box. Five out of six harvests you log are one of those numbers, so most of the time it is a single tap and the keyboard never opens — which matters most when you are standing in the garden holding a full bowl.
The quantity box itself is unchanged and still right there, so anything that is not 1-6 (half a cup, a dozen) costs exactly what it always did.
